_why:
Three regulatory edges that carried no source and no note. All three are now written from the text of 32 CFR part 117 itself, read on 22 August 2026.

The find that matters: the carve-out is CODIFIED. The board had it sourced only to DoDM 5205.07 and DoDD 5205.07 on esd.whs.mil, which returns 403 to this session. It is also in 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3), published at 85 FR 83312 on 21 December 2020, in these words: 'The Director, DCSA, will be relieved of this oversight function for DoD special access programs (SAPs) when the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense approves a carve-out provision in accordance with DoDD 5205.07.' That is a legislative rule, not internal policy, and it is on a host that answers.

Retrieval note, corrected. www.ecfr.gov 302-redirected to unblock.federalregister.gov when I first hit it, and I took that for a permanent block. Re-probing each eCFR URL once, unhurried, returns the page itself with no redirect: the block is RATE-triggered, and I had triggered it by hammering the host. eCFR is usable if approached slowly. The renderer API at /api/renderer/v1/... returned the full 716KB of part 117 either way and is the more reliable route for a whole part.

claims.text: 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3) provides verbatim: "The Director, DCSA, will be relieved of this oversight function for DoD special access programs (SAPs) when the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense approves a carve-out provision in accordance with DoDD 5205.07, 'DoD SAP Policy'." The relief of the oversight body is therefore codified in the Code of Federal Regulations, not confined to DoD internal issuances.

edges.label: relieves it of NISP oversight
edges.note: The regulation names the office the carve-out acts on. 32 CFR 117.6(b) makes the Director, DCSA responsible for 'security oversight of the NISP as the DoD CSO', and then (b)(3) removes it: "The Director, DCSA, will be relieved of this oversight function for DoD special access programs (SAPs) when the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense approves a carve-out provision in accordance with DoDD 5205.07, 'DoD SAP Policy'." So the effect is not that oversight passes to another body but that the cognizant security office's oversight function ceases for that programme, on the written approval of one of two named officials.
